---
title: "Method notes"
---

## How values are assigned

1. **Reproject.** The land cover raster is reprojected to the equal-area EPSG:6933
   with nearest-neighbor resampling, and the output uses the same grid.
2. **Overlay.** The bundled ecological zones are clipped to the boundary and
   rasterized, giving each pixel a land cover class and a zone polygon.
3. **Cross-reference.** A crosswalk links each MODIS/IGBP class to a GLC2000 class.
4. **Look up.** Each class and zone pair is matched to the Ruesch & Gibbs table by
   GLC2000 class, region, ecological zone and frontier status.
5. **Apply fallback rules.** Rules fill the values the lookup can't provide.
6. **Assign zero.** Anything still without a value receives 0.

Every row in the carbon table records how its value was set in `VALUE_SOURCE`:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lookup` | Matched in the lookup table |
| `rule` | Set by a fallback rule, named in the `RULE` column |
| `global` | Taken from a `Global` row, only with `--use-global-classes` |
| `unmatched` | No match or rule, so the value is 0 |

## Fallback rules

| Classes | Value when the lookup has none | Setting |
|---|---|---|
| Woody savannas, savannas (8, 9) | 40% of the forest reference value | `savanna_percent_of_forest` |
| Permanent wetlands (11) | The forest reference value | `wetland_woody_equals_forest` |
| Permanent wetlands (11), if no forest reference exists | The shrub reference value | `marsh_equals_shrub` |

The forest reference is the unweighted mean of the lookup values across the
country's overlay rows for classes 1 to 4. Because there is one row per class and
zone polygon, the reference depends on how many polygons the country has and not
on the area they cover. The shrub reference works the same way, for classes 6 and 7.

## Carbon table

The carbon table is the main product, because it keeps each zone's own value. Its
`Aggregated` sheet combines rows from different polygons of the same class and zone,
summing pixels and total carbon, and taking the maximum of the carbon values. Rows in
a group normally have the same value, and blank values are kept as groups.

## InVEST tables

The InVEST tables are included for completeness. InVEST assigns one value per land cover code, so each class's zone-specific values
have to be reduced to one number. Both versions are always written:

- **Dominant** uses the value from the overlay row with the most pixels.
- **Weighted** uses the pixel-weighted mean across all the class's rows.

An InVEST total built from these tables can therefore differ from the total in the
carbon table, which uses the zone-specific values. Codes that don't appear in the
country receive 0.

## Known limitations {#known-limitations}

These are kept by default so that results reproduce earlier deliveries. `polopt-carbon
check` and `run` report those that affect your country.

### Croplands and barren land receive 0

The lookup stores croplands (5 t C/ha), barren land (1 t C/ha), and water, snow, ice
and artificial surfaces (0 t C/ha) in rows with `REGION` set to `Global`. The join
uses each pixel's real region, so these rows never match, and the classes receive 0.

Code from October 2025 applied these rows through a separate step that was removed
in January 2026. Results from before and after that change can therefore differ.

`--use-global-classes` applies the rows wherever these classes occur, including in
`Water` zones. For Uganda 2023:

| | Default | With `--use-global-classes` |
|---|---|---|
| Croplands | 0 t C | 14.74 Mt C |
| Barren land | 0 t C | 0.01 Mt C |
| Total | 1,038.08 Mt C | 1,052.83 Mt C |

### Label typo in the lookup

Grassland and permanent wetland rows use `Temperate oceanic forests`, while the zones
use `Temperate oceanic forest`. Those classes receive 0 in these zones. This doesn't
affect Uganda. `--use-global-classes` also corrects this label.

### Land in water zones

The zones include `Water`, `No data` and `None`, which have no lookup rows. Most land
pixels in these zones, often along shorelines, receive 0. Savannas and wetlands are
different, because their fallback rules apply there. Wetlands in `Water` zones can
therefore receive far more carbon than wetlands elsewhere: in Uganda, 117 against 3
to 4 t C/ha.

### Carbon pools

Ruesch & Gibbs values combine aboveground and belowground living biomass, and the
tool writes the total to `c_above`. InVEST totals are correct, but the split between
pools isn't available, and soil and dead matter aren't included.

The InVEST documentation lists `c_below`, `c_soil` and `c_dead` as required. If your
version rejects the two-column table, `--invest-all-pools` adds them as zeros.

## Sources

- Ruesch, A. & Gibbs, H. K. (2008). *New IPCC Tier-1 Global Biomass Carbon Map for
  the Year 2000*. Carbon Dioxide Information Analysis Center, Oak Ridge National
  Laboratory.
- [InVEST Carbon Storage documentation](https://storage.googleapis.com/releases.naturalcapitalproject.org/invest-userguide/latest/en/carbonstorage.html)
